question: What is the primary reason why newborn skin loses heat rapidly during a bath?

options.A: Newborns have too much subcutaneous fat
options.B: Infant blood vessels are fully constricted
options.C: Newborn skin is very thin and sensitive
options.D: Babies sweat more than adults do

explanation: Because a newborn's skin is thin, heat escapes easily, making rapid drying and minimal exposure essential during bathing. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T2#BMP110_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why should harsh chemical soaps be avoided when bathing elderly clients?

options.A: Older skin has reduced oil gland activity and dries out easily
options.B: Harsh soaps permanently change the natural hair color
options.C: Chemical soaps prevent the skin from absorbing oxygen
options.D: Elderly skin produces too much natural sebum

explanation: Aging skin produces less oil, so harsh soaps remove what little moisture remains, leading to painful cracks and itching. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T2#BMP110_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why is a sponge bath recommended for a newborn instead of an immersion tub bath?

options.A: Babies are too slippery to hold securely inside a plastic tub
options.B: It prevents infection around the unhealed umbilical cord stump
options.C: Newborn muscles cramp easily when placed in standing water
options.D: Immersion baths cause permanent damage to infant eyesight

explanation: Keeping the umbilical cord dry until it detaches and heals naturally protects the newborn from bacterial entry and infection. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T2#BMP110_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which direction should a midwife wipe when cleaning a female infant's perineal area during a bath?

options.A: From front to back toward the anus
options.B: From side to side across the urethral opening
options.C: In a circular motion starting at the labia minora
options.D: From the anus forward toward the pubic bone

explanation: Wiping from front to back moves fecal bacteria away from the urethra and vagina, greatly reducing the risk of urinary tract infections. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T2#BMP110_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is the single most important safety rule when bathing a toddler in a tub?

options.A: Keep the bathroom door locked from the outside
options.B: Fill the tub completely to keep the child warm
options.D: Never leave the child unattended in the water

explanation: A young child can slip and drown in just a few centimeters of water within seconds if left unsupervised. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T2#BMP110_U5_T2_h3)

question: How can a nurse or mother prevent accidental tap-water scalding during a child's bath?

options.A: Add boiling water directly to the tub to raise the room temperature
options.B: Use only scented oils instead of testing the running water
options.C: Allow the child to adjust the water knobs while sitting inside
options.D: Run cold water first and test the temperature before the child enters

explanation: Running cold water first and blending carefully prevents scalding accidents from pipes holding unexpectedly hot water. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T2#BMP110_U5_T2_h3)

question: In what order should a bed bath be performed to maintain proper hygiene standards?

options.A: From the cleanest areas to the dirtiest areas
options.B: From the lower extremities up to the face
options.C: From the posterior back outward to the chest
options.D: From the perineal region first to the arms last

explanation: Beginning with clean zones like the face and moving toward soiled areas prevents carrying microorganisms to sensitive parts of the body. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T2#BMP110_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why is it beneficial to encourage a bedridden adult client to wash their own face and arms?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for nursing documentation
options.B: It prevents nurses from checking skin integrity
options.C: It promotes independence and preserves personal self-esteem
options.D: It ensures the skin remains wet for longer periods

explanation: Allowing patients to perform parts of their own care maintains their dignity and encourages active participation in recovery. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T2#BMP110_U5_T2_h4)

question: When should a midwife wear clean gloves during a client's bath?

options.A: Whenever the bath water temperature exceeds normal limits
options.B: Only when the client refuses to use a personal towel
options.C: When washing the perineal region or handling broken skin
options.D: During the entire duration of washing the client's face

explanation: Gloves protect the caregiver from direct contact with body fluids and non-intact skin areas during hygiene care. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T2#BMP110_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard safety measure to prevent bathroom accidents in healthcare facilities?

options.A: Using rubber non-slip mats inside the shower stall
options.B: Ensuring the emergency call bell is within easy reach
options.C: Applying scented oils directly to the bathroom floor tiles
options.D: Checking on clients at regular intervals during their shower

explanation: Putting oils on the floor makes surfaces dangerously slick and increases the risk of severe slips and falls. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T2#BMP110_U5_T2_h5)
